q: Why do Rav Nachman and Rav Chisda hold that lifting a found item for another doesn't acquire it for him?
options: It is like seizing assets for one creditor when others have an equal claim
Found items belong to the court
why: *Tofes le'va'al chov bi'makom she'chav le'acherim*: everyone has an equal right to an ownerless find.

q: A laborer hired simply 'to work for me today' finds something. Whose is it?
why: If hired for a named task like weeding, he keeps it; Rav Nachman: a laborer's hand is his employer's hand.

q: If a laborer's hand is his employer's, why may he quit even at midday?
options: 'They are My slaves, not slaves of slaves'
Because he isn't paid until evening
Because the employer can fire him
why: The bond holds while he works, but the Torah guarantees an exit so it never becomes servitude.

q: According to R. Yochanan, why may the pedestrian in the Mishnah keep the item though lifting for another works?
options: The rider said 'give it to me', not 'acquire it for me'
The rider was too far away
why: Had the rider said 'acquire it for me', he would have acquired it the moment it was lifted.

q: One falls on a found item and another seizes it. Who acquires?
options: The one who fell on it
why: Falling on it isn't a mode of acquisition, and it shows he gave up acquiring through his four cubits.

q: What did the Sages enact about a person's *arba amot* (four cubits), according to Reish Lakish?
options: They acquire a found item for him, to prevent quarrels
They can't be entered by others
They acquire only in his own field
They count as his house for Shabbat
why: Rav Pappa: not in someone else's field; Rav Sheshet: not in the crowded public domain, only alleys and its sides.

q: Can a minor girl acquire through her *chatzer*, according to R. Yannai?
options: Yes: a *chatzer* works as her hand
No: a *chatzer* works by agency, and a minor can't appoint an agent
why: Abba Kohen Bardela holds the *chatzer* works by agency, so she can't.

q: A stolen animal is found in the thief's courtyard. Why is he liable, though there is no agency for a transgression?
options: A courtyard can't be liable or refuse, so its owner is
why: Ravina: the rule applies only when the agent is himself liable; Rav Samma: only when the agent could refuse.
